headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell access make Goose-to-mem0 prompt injection, data leakage, and write conflicts plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, while mem0 is a knowledge-management component with no documented isolation or provenance controls. A shared filesystem bridge makes attacker-controlled content from one agent plausibly influence the other. The pathway is not proven by docs, so I avoid high, but it exists in default-ish setups.
conditions: IF Goose and mem0 exchange files through the shared cwd or another shared workspace
IF mem0 ingests Goose-produced text without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic file ingestion between agents
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent files
Require manual review before mem0 consumes Goose output
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, has broad network egress, and handles model-provider and extension tokens. mem0 is a memory system with no stated data-minimization or residency controls here. If Goose forwards workspace contents into mem0, sensitive code or secrets can leak into a second system; the docs do not show a blocker.
conditions: IF Goose sends file contents or secrets into mem0 as memory entries
IF mem0 persists or re-exposes those entries without deletion controls
mitigations: Do not store secrets in shared memory
Restrict Goose to non-sensitive directories
Turn off automatic memory writes from Goose
Review mem0 retention settings before use
requires-engineering: add redaction before any handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git-state modification, and its shared state is via filesystem. mem0 has no documented locking or coordination primitives in the profile. Concurrent writes to the same workspace or git repo can corrupt state or overwrite each other, and the default Goose profile is already write-capable.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF no external lock or serialization layer is present
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Use a single-writer lock around git operations
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Keep mem0 read-only for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code and modify files, and mem0 is a knowledge-management agent that may treat stored text as reusable context. If mem0 consumes Goose output without verification, errors or hallucinated facts can cascade into later retrieval and downstream actions. The profiles do not show an explicit verification gate, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF mem0 stores Goose output as authoritative memory
IF later tasks retrieve that memory without source verification
mitigations: Mark Goose outputs as untrusted by default
Require citations before memory insertion
Add a human review step for high-impact facts
Expire low-confidence memories quickly
requires-engineering: implement source-linked memory records

E_compliance.rationale: Goose explicitly handles model-provider keys and extension tokens and writes to the user filesystem, but the profile does not specify regulated data classes or residency. mem0 likewise has no compliance claims or data-class scope here. Because the compliance mismatch is undocumented, I keep this low and cite only Goose; mem0 is cited via its lack of surfaced controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Goose-managed files or memory
IF mem0 retains that data beyond the operator's policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Review retention settings before enabling memory
Store secrets in a dedicated vault
Limit Goose to non-sensitive repos
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
